[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Close-outcome letter aliases (x → !, s → *) in Bob Mac Capture[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]In the Bob Mac Capture editor, a plain lowercase `x` typed where a [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]close selection accepts an outcome marker becomes `!`, and a plain [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]lowercase `s` becomes `*`. Examples: `xx` → `x!`, `xs` → `x*`, [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]`x1s` → `x1*`, `x=1=s` → `x=1=*`, and `@r:id=xx` → `@r:id=x!`. [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]Bob's `capture-rewrite` alone decides where the alias fires. `bob [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]capture`, `capture-parse`, paste, and CLI text keep the letters. [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]Typing speed never changes the outcome: keys typed before Bob [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]answers are held and replayed, and a fast Return never files the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]literal draft.[/#D7D7AF]
